question: Which folk dance of Punjab is mainly performed by women?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Giddha.**__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__****Giddha**:

__
 
• It is a well-liked folk dance performed by females in the **Punjab **area.
 
• It is **distinct **from other types of Punjabi traditional dance.
 
• It is not necessary to perform the two-headed barrel dhol drum.
 
• It **depicts **the histories of women's lives, encompassing **domestic life, marriage, and homesickness.**
 
• Other **Punjab folk dances **are:
 
 
• Bhangra.
 
• Luddi.
 
• Kikkli.
 
• Sammi.
 
• Gatka(Dankara).
 
• Jhumar.
 
• Jaago.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__****Jawara**:

 
• It is performed by both **men and women**.
 
• It is a **Madhya Pradesh** folk dance.
 
• It is mostly done by the peasant communities in the **Bundelkhand region.** 
 
• It is one of the harvest dances in the region.
 
• Other **Madhya Pradesh folk dances **include:
 
 
• Matki.
 
• Aada.
 
• Khada Nach.
 
• Phulpati.
 
• rida Dance.
 
• Selalarke.
 
• Selabhadoni.
 
• Maanch.
 
 

**Dadra**:

 
• It is a folk dance from **Uttar Pradesh.**
 
• It is performed by courtesans.
 
• It is mainly a **celebration of marriage **and physical pleasures.
 
• Other **folk dances in Uttar Pradesh **are:
 
 
• Charkula.
 
• Kajri.
 
• Kathak.
 
• Khyal.
 
• Nautanki.
 
• Ramlila.
 
• Raslila.
 
 

**Fugdi**:

 
• It is a folk dance **from Goa and Maharashtra**.
 
• It is **performed by women **of tribal, Hindu, and Christian communities.
 
• It is performed with the sounds of women clapping.
 
• List of **folk dances in Goa and Maharashtra**:

 
 

 **State/UT**
 **Folk Dance**
 
 

 **Goa**
 Dekhni, Dashavatara, Dhalo, Dhangar, Goff, Kunbi, Divlyan Nach, Veerbhadra, Romta Mel, Correndinho, Ghodemodni.
 
 

 **Maharashtra**
 Lavani, Dhangarigaja, Lezim, Koli, Tamasha, Povadas, Dindi and Kala
